title: Fluency
goal: Combine everything: pick the shortest path for real edits without thinking about the keys.

lessons.title: Refactoring a code block

concepts.desc: change exactly the piece you mean: a word, inside brackets, up to a character.
substitute on this line; & repeats the last :s on another line (g& on all lines).
in a pattern, escape [ ] to match them literally (items\[i\]).
land on punctuation in one jump, then repeat.
repeat the last change; with * or n, step to the next match and repeat it.

lessons.tip: Before you start, decide on the plan: which parts are text objects (ci(), which are patterns (:s), which are one-offs (cw). The plan matters more than typing speed.

quiz.q: Replace everything inside the parentheses on this line with `x`.
quiz.a: f( then ci(x<Esc> (ci( also works with the cursor already inside).

quiz.q: Repeat the last :s on the current line.
Repeat the last :s, with the same flags, on every line.
Pattern that matches the literal text `items[i]`.
Change `var` to `let` in 5 places spread through a file, using * and .
quiz.a: * on var (or /var), cw let<Esc>, then n. n. n. ...

quiz.q: Change from the cursor up to (not including) the next `;`.

lessons.title: Reshaping data: logs to CSV

concepts.desc: delete every line that does NOT match (same as :g!/pat/d).
capture groups reorder fields in one pass.
one field (a run of non-space characters).
sort lines alphabetically / by number / and drop duplicates.
write (a|b)+ without backslashes: :%s/\v(\S+) (\S+)/\2 \1/

lessons.tip: For data reshaping, think in whole-buffer commands: filter (:g/:v), transform (:s), order (:sort). Three commands, any number of lines.

quiz.q: Delete all lines that don't contain ERROR.
Swap two space-separated words on every line.
Sort lines numerically.
Sort and remove duplicate lines.
What does \v at the start of a pattern change?
quiz.a: Very magic: ( ) | + ? { have their special meaning without backslashes.

quiz.q: Copy every line containing TODO to the end of the file.

lessons.title: Rewriting a config format

concepts.desc: alternation in a group: match a or b.
one or more digits.
fix the last line, open a line above the first, open one below the last.
remove all indent on this line / one level less / one level more, while typing.
substitute only in the visual selection.
reselect the last visual selection, to run a second command on the same lines.

lessons.tip: Do the bulk change first, then patch the exceptions (the last comma, the wrapping braces). Don't try to write one perfect regex.

quiz.q: Remove the quotes around values that are digits or true/false.
Delete the last character of the last line of the file.
Run a substitution only on the lines you just selected visually.
quiz.a: :'<,'>s/.../.../ (press : in visual mode to get the range)

quiz.q: Reselect the previous visual selection.
Indent the entire file by one level.
In a pattern, what does \| do?
quiz.a: Alternation: match the left OR the right side.

lessons.title: Macros at scale

concepts.desc: record into register a / replay / replay the last macro.
run until it fails: the macro stops at the first motion that can't move (e.g. j on the last line).
run a macro on every line / each selected line.

concepts.keys: I / A / e / w in macros
concepts.desc: use motions that work on every line regardless of length; avoid counting with l.
paste a macro, edit it as text, yank it back into the register.

lessons.tip: Start the macro by getting to a known position (I, 0, ^) and end it on the next line with j. Then it's safe to replay any number of times.

quiz.q: Replay macro a on every line of the file.
Why is `100@a` safe on a 12-line file?
quiz.a: The macro aborts as soon as a command fails (like j/↓ on the last line), so the extra runs never happen.

quiz.q: How do you fix a typo inside the recorded macro a?
quiz.a: "ap to paste it, edit the text, then 0"ay$ (or "add) to yank it back; :let @a='...' also works.

quiz.q: Replay the last macro you ran.
Why prefer `e` or `f,` over `lllll` inside a macro?
quiz.a: Lines differ in length; motions based on text structure work on every line, fixed column counts don't.

quiz.q: Append to an existing macro in register a.

lessons.title: Graduation: your own cheat sheet

concepts.desc: insert a shell command's output below the cursor.
reflow text to 'textwidth'.
random replay of a past drill. Keep a weekly habit.
community challenges to keep improving after the course.

lessons.tip: Mastery is a habit, not a finish line: one vimgolf challenge or one vimdrill --review a week keeps it sharp, and :help is where you look next.

quiz.q: Insert the output of `date` below the cursor.
Reflow the current paragraph.
quiz.a: gqip (or gwip to keep the cursor in place)

quiz.q: Lowercase a whole paragraph.
Delete every blank line in the file.
Search help for anything mentioning 'textwidth'.
Swap two adjacent lines.
